axes.model_access: The platform ships no in-house model — models are integrated per scenario; the homepage does not lead with a model picker, and the model list is not verified item by item. The product is packaged as an "AI employee": 40+ built-in Skills, teachable custom skills (same-day homepage on record).
axes.runtime: Cloud-hosted form (www.lindy.ai direct 200; Chrome Extension integrated with Gmail on record); no official self-hosted distribution found, treated as unknown.
axes.local_files: Data lives in Lindy's cloud (Memory — "Remembers you. Yours to edit" — is the cloud persistent surface); the local-file concept does not apply — work artifacts (emails, docs, call records) land in third-party tools (Gmail/calendar/CRM) via integrations rather than on your machine.
axes.background: "Routines: Work that runs on schedule" is the official lead form (same-day homepage on record) — scheduled autonomous runs are the product's main axis; Watch and Learn (show it once, it takes over) on record; queueing and retry details not verified item by item.
axes.tools: Integration surface on record same day: 1,500+ integrations + MCP (the homepage states MCP explicitly); Lindy Phone (calls) and Lindy Apps are new product lines (on record in both the terms and the changelog); a phone-compliance clause section is on record same day.
axes.context: Memory is the explicit persistent surface (same-day homepage: "Remembers you. Yours to edit" — user-editable memory); the Meetings shared library is on record; memory scoping and retention details not verified item by item.
axes.permissions: The terms contain a dedicated phone-compliance section (recording/consent obligations for Lindy Phone fall on the user, on record same day); the terms use a generic commercial template (the entity is just "Company"); training-use toggle path not verified item by item.
axes.fit: Fits: email/calendar/call/CRM "AI employee" automation (scheduled routines, learn-by-demonstration), 1,500+ integrations with MCP. Not a fit: self-hosting, a filed direct-mainland entry, code-level control (the product form is a hired agent, not a canvas or code).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to agent platforms).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Failure handling and audit surface of Routines** (who sees errors from scheduled autonomous runs, and how to roll back — not on record)
- **Memory scoping boundaries** (shared across agents or per-agent; retention period not on record)
- **Lindy Phone connect rates and compliance interception** (the terms push obligations onto the user; actual call quality and interception not verified)
unknowns:
- The integrated model list (not verified item by item)
- Self-hosting/private deployment form (no official statement verified)
- Training-use toggle path and default state (not verified item by item)
- Full legal entity name (the terms only self-describe as Lindy/Oregon, no Inc./LLC)
related: Also a workflow-agent platform: Gumloop is a canvas+connectors form, Lindy is a hired "AI employee" form.
Integration-automation contrast: n8n's node canvas is self-hostable under fair-code; Lindy is fully hosted and speaks the language of an "employee".
Delegation-form contrast: ChatGPT is a general chat entry you drive; Lindy is an always-on "employee" it drives itself — same natural-language briefs, different runtime model.
